# What you have after installing cjw_multisite

This page describes a new installation made with `cjw_multisite` and the languages `eng-US` and `ger-DE`: what is on
the screen, what is in the content tree and the database, and which files the installer wrote. It is for the
administrator or host who has just run the install and wants to check it, and for website creators who start
building on the starter site. Each item names the code that made it, so you can look it up in
[The installer scripts](the-installer-scripts.md).

## Contents

1. [The addresses](#the-addresses)
2. [The content tree](#the-content-tree)
3. [Tags, layouts and paths](#tags-layouts-and-paths)
4. [Sections, user groups and roles](#sections-user-groups-and-roles)
5. [The settings files written](#the-settings-files-written)
6. [Extensions and tables](#extensions-and-tables)
7. [What is not there](#what-is-not-there)
8. [A first look: check list](#a-first-look-check-list)
9. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## The addresses

With URL access on `https://www.example.com`:

| Address | Siteaccess | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `https://www.example.com/` | `site` (`DefaultAccess`) | the start page of the starter site, in the primary language |
| `https://www.example.com/ger/` | `ger` | the same site in German |
| `https://www.example.com/admin/` | `admin` | the administration, design `admin4l` |
| `https://www.example.com/editor/` | `editor` | the administration for editors |
| `https://www.example.com/adminui/` | `adminui` | the AdminUI design, when `exp_adminui` is installed |

The site name (`[SiteSettings] SiteName`) is what you typed, or **CJW JAC Exponential** when you
left it empty or kept a default. The commit of 2026-10-11 made the starter content use the same name throughout: the
site info's site name in English and German, the front page's title and meta title, the footer, the imprint and the
cookie policy title.

A live example of the result is listed on [Demo sites](../../designers/distribution/demo-sites.md).

## The content tree

| Node | Remote id | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | `cjw-starter-n-root` | directly below the content root; the content root (`RootNode`) and `PathPrefix` of the public siteaccesses |
| Start page ("Startseite", `ng_frontpage`) | `cjw-starter-n-779` | the `IndexPage` and `DefaultPage` of the public siteaccesses |
| The configuration folder | `cjw-starter-n-807` | hidden; holds the site info, the cookie policy and the header links |
| The privacy page ("Datenschutzerklärung") | `cjw-starter-n-809` | `menu.ini [SiteInfo] PrivacyPolicyID` and `CookiePolicyID` |

Below the root: 137 objects from `cjw_multisite_democontent`, among them 61 images, 23 articles, 9 news items, 6
banners and 5 galleries, landing pages, containers and shortcuts each (see
[The demo content package](the-demo-content-package.md#the-content-objects)). Their publish dates are those of the
source site. The administration starts at the content root (node 2), so it shows the starter tree and the rest of
the base data.

## Tags, layouts and paths

- **Tags**: a tag "Starter" (`cjw-starter-t-root`) with the five tags of `cjw-starter-import.json` below it, linked
  to the eztags fields of the starter objects.
- **Starter layouts**: 23 layouts (6 of them shared), 113 zones, 269 blocks and 11 rules with ids from 900000, from
  `cjw-explayouts.json`. Their siteaccess rules name `site` and `ger`.
- **Admin layouts**: `admin_3col`, `admin_2col` and `admin_full` with their zones, blocks and rules, ids from 100001,
  from `extension/explayouts/share/fragments/admin_layouts_db_data.dba`, loaded only when none exists.
- **URL paths**: the paths of the source site per language (`cjw-paths.json`); renamed elements leave a history entry
  that redirects (301) to the new path.

## Sections, user groups and roles

| Item | What the installer did |
|---|---|
| Section **Restricted** | created; given to the user group Partners and to the base data's Archives folder |
| User group **Partners** | created under Users; assigned the roles Partner, Member and Anonymous |
| User group **Members** | the base data's "Guest accounts" group, renamed; assigned Member |
| Editors | assigned Member as well |
| Anonymous | `rss/feed`, `user/login` on every served siteaccess except `admin` and `adminui`, `content/read` in section 3 (Media), `tags/view`, `info-collection/read`, `osm_proxy/tiles`, `shop/buy` and the content policies of the 7x installer |
| Member | `content/read` in section 3, `tags/view`, `info-collection/read`, `osm_proxy/tiles` and its own content policies |
| Editor | the editor policies of the 7x installer; the commit history adds node data calls guarded by a policy, `uiswitch/language` and `uiswitch/design` |
| Two-step sign-in | `user2fa/setup` and `user2fa/verify` for Member, Editor and Partner when `sevenx_authentication_2fa` is installed |

There is also an RSS export, **My RSS Feed** at `my_feed`, with up to ten `ng_article` objects from below the starter
root.

The roles of the 7x installer are described in detail in
[Roles and policies of sevenx_multisite](../sevenx-multisite/roles-and-policies.md).

## The settings files written

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `settings/override/site.ini.append.php` | siteaccess lists, `MatchOrder`, `ForceVirtualHost=true`, `ActiveExtensions[]`, the database settings, cache headers for anonymous visitors, session handler |
| `settings/override/ezurlmultisite.ini.append.php` | the public siteaccesses and their root nodes, for links between sites |
| `settings/siteaccess/site/` | `site.ini`, `content.ini` (`RootNode`), `menu.ini`, `override.ini` and the other files of `siteINISettings()` |
| `settings/siteaccess/ger/` | the copy for German |
| `settings/siteaccess/admin/`, `editor/`, `adminui/` | the administration |

The siteaccesses the installer writes get `[SearchSettings] LogSearchStats=enabled`; the public ones get
`[SiteAccessRules]` that switch the `ezinfo` module off.

## Extensions and tables

`ActiveExtensions[]` is the list of `sevenx_multisite` plus `cjw_themes_jumper` and `cjw_tmv`, ending with
`ezurlmultisite`. The admin gets `expai` and `exp_adminui` as access extensions where present; `expai` is switched
off and has no provider keys. The tables of every listed extension with a schema were created from that schema
alone: no extension `db_data.dba` was loaded. The starter's layout and tag rows come from the starter content steps,
the admin layouts from their own fragment.

## What is not there

- No second site: no `bold` or other secondary siteaccess.
- No rows from `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_data.dba` or `extension/explayouts/share/db_data.dba`: the
  starter layouts come from the content package instead.
- No images in the package repository: after the install the links into `extension/cjw_themes_jumper/share/` are
  removed again; the images live in the site's storage.

## A first look: check list

- [ ] `/` shows the start page in the `starter` design, with the site name in the title.
- [ ] `/ger/` shows the German site; the language switcher offers both languages.
- [ ] Images show on the start page and in the galleries (if not, see the note below).
- [ ] `/admin/` shows the administration; Content structure has the node "Starter".
- [ ] Layouts in the administration list the "Starter - ..." layouts.
- [ ] The privacy page link in the cookie banner opens "Datenschutzerklärung".
- [ ] The setup's debug output has no line "Starter content steps that failed".

> **Note**
> Missing images almost always mean `extension/cjw_themes_jumper` (with its `share/` folders) was not in place during
> the install. The log then has "Files of the starter content not found in extension/cjw_themes_jumper/share".

> **Tip**
> Built a site of your own on this starter? Package it and contribute it: 7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly
> encourage it. See [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).
